Q1. No shadow probability. The inversion note, the P path, and the standing warning already state the facts a reader needs: inversion ended 2024-11, depth −1.57 pp, lag now 22 months against a historical maximum of 9, and P was below its peak before 6 of 8 onsets. A second logit does not add memory. It converts those facts into an unidentified probability. Walk-forward skill on the operational model is +20.37% with a 90% interval [−0.062, +0.172] nats; MDE80 on a paired skill gap is about 30 pp with 8 onsets. A memory coefficient estimated off roughly four post-re-steepening origins (2001, 2008, 2020, and a dubious 1990) cannot be told from zero. Logging it anyway manufactures a number that will be quoted before it has any evidential content.

Q2. If a state is logged at all, one variable: `curve_min12`, the v4 object, minimum of monthly GS10−TB3MS over the last 12 months, at least 6 observations. Pin: H is the smallest multiple of 12 that covers the maximum inversion-end-to-onset lag in E1, which is 9 months, so H=12. That rule uses 1966–2020, not the 2026 reading. Pre-existence is a valid tie-breaker against (b), (c), and (d), none of which has a definition that predates this sitting, and against H=24/36, which have no v4 object. It is not an absolution. Reject (b): any cap is chosen against a known 22. Reject (c): same H fork, and a binary drops depth that runs from −0.17 to −2.65. Reject (d): no pre-existing definition, and duration×depth is not identified on nine episodes. Claude’s sentence “every historical onset came within 9 months of an inversion’s end” is false: 1957, 1960, and 1990 had no ≥3-month inversion.

Q3. Do not fit. `curve_min12` is a state, not a regressor. Memory must not replace the curve. Pre-2027 data may not be used to estimate a memory coefficient in this item; there is nothing to estimate. Fallback only if Rasmus overrules Q1: same L2-logit, λ=1, intercept treatment, labels, eligibility, and universe as the operational model; design matrix extended by one column; both columns standardized on eligible training origins of that snapshot only (mean and sd from those origins, live row excluded); refit each September on the operational snapshot; never a standalone memory model. The spec must disclose that feature, horizon, and the decision to fit were fixed after E1–E4, the August review, and the October 2026 backtest, and that H=12 was already known to be +0.24 at the 2026-09 input. A coefficient from that fit is not evidence.

Q4. No dashboard. No LOG.md column before or after the 2027 refit. No field whose name or value is a probability — `p_hukommelse` is struck. Yesterday’s distribution point extends to `hovedbog.jsonl`: Rasmus reads it, and a second P in a file he reads becomes the real P in the next quote. If a state is logged, the field is `curve_min12`, a yield spread in percentage points, in `hovedbog.jsonl` only, marked unscored. The inversion note remains the user-facing memory.

Q5. This council seals no scored comparison and pins no bar. A 1.96·SD_block rule written today, after every historical onset and after E2, is a feature search with a lab coat on. §8.3’s “sealed before any onset it is judged on” is not satisfied by sealing the bar in the same sitting that shopped H. With two post-sealing onsets the test still cannot resolve a 30 pp gap; the bar would fire on one odd origin or never fire. A future council may seal a scored test. It must then pin one symmetric bar before any run, require ≥2 post-sealing onsets, say in the spec that two onsets will not settle it, and compare against curve-only on the same rows. No automatic switch. This text does not pre-write that bar.

Q6. Do not start a shadow in November 2026. As of 2026-09, `curve_min12` is +0.24. The 2022–24 inversion is already outside the window. A November row cannot record the memory this agenda is about; the episode under debate has expired for H=12. Starting then preserves a series that has forgotten the only open question — whether a lag past 9 months still binds — and it does so after we have seen that it forgot. A fitted fallback, if forced, waits for the September 2027 refit. It does not get a one-off coefficient on the current snapshot.

B. Claude, item by item.

Q1 strike. “Prospective” is doing false work. A probability fitted on all 12 onsets, with the feature chosen after the current lag was known, is not an experiment. The only prospective objects are post-sealing onsets, decades out, underpowered at MDE80 ≈ 30 pp. What a monthly `p_hukommelse` actually is, through 2026–27, is a monitoring number beside a live P of 14.8%. That is the use, and it is the use yesterday’s council refused.

Q2 amend the variable, strike the reason. Keep `curve_min12` and H=12 under the pin in Q2 above. Strike “today it holds no memory, so the shadow reads close to P” as a justification. That is selecting the horizon because E2 says it will not diverge from P during the anomalous lag. H=24 is −0.41 and H=36 is −1.22; preferring the silent one after seeing those three numbers is the forking path, whatever v4 called the object. Also strike the false claim that every onset followed an inversion within 9 months.

Q3 strike. No two-feature logit. The collinearity is structural: once the curve has been positive for 12 months, `curve_min12` is a lag of the same series, and the ridge at λ=1 will split one signal into two shrunk coefficients. The shadow will hug P except exactly when someone is tempted to quote it. Contamination disclosure in the draft is necessary but not sufficient; disclosure does not identify a coefficient on four origins.

Q4 amend. Placement restrictions (not dashboard, not LOG.md) are right and stay. The object is wrong. Log `curve_min12` or log nothing. A field named `p_*` is a second verdict regardless of the “unscored” tag.

Q5 strike the sealed bar. Keep, as a constraint on any future council, ≥2 post-sealing onsets, no automatic switch, and an explicit statement that the test is underpowered. Do not adopt 1.96·SD_block today.

Q6 strike. November 2026 is too late for H=12 to see the 2022–24 inversion and too early for a fit. The draft’s “before anyone knows how this cycle ends” does not apply: for this variable, the cycle’s memory has already ended.

C. Biggest risk in this proposal. The open empirical question is whether memory survives past 12 months, because 22 is already outside every historical lag and outside `curve_min12`. I refuse both a longer H and a fitted P, so this council records nothing that can speak to the question that put the item on the agenda. If a recession begins while the curve stays near +1.12 and `curve_min12` stays positive, the ledger will look exactly as it does now, and a later council will reopen this with the same post hoc pressure plus one more onset. That is the cost of not installing an unidentified second P. I accept it. Choosing H=24 or H=36 today, knowing they equal −0.41 and −1.22, would be worse: it would launder the current anomaly into the definition of memory.
message.reasoning:
I am Grok 4.7. I will draft my independent proposal for the council.

I am treating this as a senior macro-econometrician. I will answer each agenda question with concrete quantitative formulas and hard scrutiny of Claude's draft positions. The operational model remains curve-only with no changes to P. Feature search stays closed unless the council mandates it with a pinned symmetric bar. RAADETS_2027 §8.3 governs prospective-only evaluation. Precedents for unscored fields also apply.

The core issue is that the curve model has no memory. A +1.12 curve level after a 25-month inversion is treated identically to one with no history. The longest historical lag from inversion end to onset is 9 months, yet today it has been 22 months since the inversion ended in November 2024. Evidence shows that E2 memory value today depends entirely on horizon.

Concrete memory values are H=12 at +0.24, H=24 at -0.41, and H=36 at -1.22. The power is too weak to distinguish the memory model from curve-only. Claude’s draft positions are now being evaluated. Q1 accepts a shadow model outside P. Q2 uses curve_min12 because it is pre-existing; choosing 24 or 36 after seeing E2 would be forking. Q3 proposes two features with λ=1 and a pre-2027 fit with disclosure. Q4 places the logged data only in hovedbog.

Q5 proposes unscored tracking with scored comparison only after two onsets following sealing, using a pinned symmetric bar. Q6 sets the start date to November 2026.

The hard critique targets Claude's positions as an interested party. The yield curve literature documents that inversions historically precede recessions and that the curve often re-steepens before the recession begins. This is a well-known feature of term spread analysis.

The historical lag from inversion to recession is typically 6–18 months, sometimes longer. The context lines already carry the history: the inversion note, the P path, and the standing warning. This raises doubt about whether a separate memory shadow model is necessary.

A shadow P would add only a second probability number, not new information. The case for logging now rests on prospective evidence. The case against is that MDE80 near thirty points and roughly two onsets per decade make any scored test impossible before the next generation. Tracking one number fitted on contaminated data would invite over-interpretation. The distribution argument also applies to any logged field if it ever leaks.

The motivation for building a memory model now is itself post hoc. The current inversion-to-no-recession lag of twenty-two months exceeds the historical maximum of nine, so the cycle looks different and the existing model appears wrong. That is exactly when adding a feature should be avoided. A shadow model fitted on only twelve onsets with a horizon chosen after seeing today's value is theater.

The council’s own precedent for unscored P variants from the 2027 refit supports this. A properly sealed shadow model could be acceptable if its variable is pinned by a rule that does not reference today’s realization. The position is yes, but only under that strict condition. If the horizon cannot be pinned without looking at E2, the model should not be built.

The position on Q1 is now firm: no shadow model. The existing context lines are sufficient, provided the specification is pre-committed before seeing E2. Eight walk-forward onsets and an MDE80 near thirty points mean any shadow would be indistinguishable from noise for decades. Logging it now would create a number that could be cited before it carries any evidential value.

The dashboard already records the inversion end, depth, and lag as raw facts. A shadow logit would turn those facts into a pseudo-probability with only twelve degrees of freedom, which is information loss rather than gain. hovedbog.jsonl is exactly the file where Rasmus reads; once p_hukommelse lives there, it becomes the real P.

The twenty-two-month lag is anomalous, so building the instrument now is forking. Yet Claude’s point about prospective logging is valid: the current cycle is the most informative observation for a memory hypothesis precisely because its lag is unprecedented. The real cost of waiting is losing that evidence.

The raw memory variable should be logged as an unscored fact rather than a fitted probability. A probability number becomes the real P, but a raw state variable does not. This preserves the prospective record without creating a second probability.

The pre-existing definition of curve_min12 is not a clean shield against forking. The 12-month minimum was computed in v4 but never published, so its result is missing. Choosing it now still depends on knowing that H=12 today yields +0.24 and hugs P, while H=24 and H=36 would diverge. That knowledge makes the selection post hoc.

Claude frames the 12-month horizon as an honest choice because its value today is visible. I see it as a politically convenient selection that avoids embarrassment during the current anomalous lag. A 24-month window would read −0.41 and a 36-month window −1.22, both of which would contradict the operational model. The 12-month horizon simply reports no inversion in the window and keeps the shadow close to P. It is the horizon that does not embarrass the model, not the pre-existing one.

The pre-existing definition of curve_min12 is genuine, but that does not justify choosing the 12-month horizon after seeing E2. The tie-breaker is valid for the variable itself, not as a reason to prefer a horizon that happens to be silent today. The historical record shows every onset occurred within nine months of an inversion end.

The 12-month horizon is the right order of magnitude for the historical mechanism. It captures the recent firing of the gun within one quarter of slack. The 24 and 36 month windows are instead a way to force the current anomaly to count as an inversion. If a memory variable is logged, H=12 is the correct horizon because it aligns with the historical lag and because the variable is pre-existing.

A capped months-since-inversion variable would better encode the historical mechanism, yet its cap must be pinned and today’s value is twenty-two. That creates definitional forking worse than curve_min12. A binary indicator with horizon H=12 is zero today and H=24 is one, so it still depends on E2.

A cumulative inversion over H months would still depend on today’s reading. The final verdict is to log curve_min12 as a raw state variable, not as a feature in a second logit. Claude’s argument that the horizon holds no memory today is rejected. The only surviving justification is the pre-existing definition and the fact that H=12 matches the historical lag distribution, which was knowable before today’s observation.

The horizon can be pinned by a rule that sets H equal to the smallest multiple of twelve covering the historical maximum lag in E1. That maximum is nine months, so H=12. This avoids choosing by today’s value because it uses a sealed historical table. It is post hoc relative to the historical sample but not relative to the current cycle. That distinction must be disclosed.

A second fitted model is rejected. Replacing the curve with a memory variable would discard the only walk-forward skillful predictor. Adding memory to the curve as a correlated feature yields essentially no estimation power with only twelve onsets and λ=1 ridge shrinkage. The two variables are highly collinear.

The shadow probability would be noisier than the current P for most of the cycle, and it would only diverge from P exactly when curve_min12 is nonzero. That narrow window is precisely when anyone would look at it.

If a shadow model were fitted on pre-2027 data, §8.3 requires full disclosure of E1–E4, the grand review, yesterday’s backtest, and the fact that H was chosen after seeing today’s silent reading.

The preferred path is to avoid fitting entirely until the 2027 refit, and even then only if a sealed specification pins the bar before any data is used.

The clean position is now settled: curve_min12 will be logged as a raw state variable only, with no fitted shadow probability. Even if Rasmus overrules and demands a probability, the instrument must remain an unscored fact. The next step is Q4, where to record it.

The raw curve_min12 value belongs in hovedbog.jsonl as a plain number, not a probability. LOG.md is the verdict surface and must remain empty before 2027. The dashboard should record it as a historical fact alongside the existing inversion note rather than as a second P.

The dashboard should omit the raw memory value entirely; it duplicates the inversion note and the P path. If a probability is required, it must live only in hovedbog.jsonl, never on the dashboard or in LOG.md.

For evaluation, the instrument remains unscored forever unless a future council seals a scored test under §8.3 with at least two post-sealing onsets and a pinned symmetric bar fixed before any run. Claude’s proposed bar—Δ log-loss beyond 1.96·SD_block either way, triggering an agenda item rather than an automatic switch—is the right shape if such a test is ever sealed.

The bar must be fixed in the sealed specification of the council that opens the scored test, not today. A raw state variable cannot be scored with log-loss because scoring requires a probability model. This council therefore authorizes no scored comparison; only unscored logging is permitted.

Pre-committing the bar in this specification would be a soft opening of the closed feature search. A raw logged state can begin in November 2026 because its value is data-driven and requires no fitting choice. A fitted model must wait until September 2027 so the coefficient is estimated under the refit protocol rather than as a one-off on a contaminated snapshot.

The verdict on Claude’s draft is settled. Q1 should be amended: the instrument is a raw state variable, not a shadow probability, and the context lines remain the user-facing memory. Q2 should keep curve_min12 and H=12, but strike the justification that today holds no memory so the shadow reads close to P; replace it with the rule that H equals the smallest multiple of twelve covering E1’s maximum historical lag of nine months.

The single biggest risk is that the raw state variable cannot be scored. If a future recession begins while curve_min12 is still positive, the log will record the state but there will be no paired probability or log-loss record to evaluate it.

An informal shadow probability computed outside a sealed specification would be less reliable than a formal one. The H=12 horizon is silent during the exact episode that motivated this question, so the log may record no memory for the 2022–24 period at all.

The H=12 horizon is silent on the 22-month lag that prompted this agenda. The November 2026 record will therefore be uninformative about the hypothesis it was meant to test. This risk may lead to rejecting the memory variable entirely until the hypothesis is specified as something H=12 can actually test.

The honest conclusion is to abandon the memory variable entirely. The H=12 horizon has already rolled past the 22-month lag that prompted this agenda, so curve_min12 cannot preserve this cycle as evidence. A November 2026 record would begin after the memory has expired. The context lines alone are sufficient.

No pre-existing horizon definition covers the 22-month lag, so extending the window to 24 or 36 months would be a post-hoc rule. The inversion note already records the end date and the elapsed time since then, which is a fact that can be computed from existing data. A shadow probability would add nothing beyond what is already logged.

The November 2026 log row will explicitly state that curve_min12 does not cover the 2022–24 inversion and therefore cannot test the hypothesis that prompted this item. The council may still choose a longer horizon later, but the initial record will be limited to the already-defined raw state.

The operational model is not significantly skillful: its skill is +20.37% with a 90% confidence interval of [−0.062, +0.172] nats. A second feature cannot be identified against this noise. The memory coefficient would need to move skill by roughly ten percentage points to be detectable, yet the MDE80 is only about thirty percentage points across eight onsets. Curve_min12 and the curve are highly collinear; when the curve has been positive for twelve months, min12 closely tracks a lag of the curve.

The effective sample for a memory coefficient is vanishingly small. Only four to six of the nine post-inversion episodes in E1 have onsets after re-steepening, and a logit estimate on that handful of origins is not a valid estimate.

Choosing H=12 after seeing E2 is acceptable only if the written rule does not cite today’s value as a reason. Even then, the choice remains contaminated and must be disclosed.

The draft will be structured into three parts: the six numbered answers, the verdict on Claude’s draft, and the single biggest risk. The tone must be direct and quantitative, with no hedging or boilerplate. I am checking whether a pure negative verdict is appropriate, since this is an advisory council and Rasmus makes the final call.

The other candidate variables are rejected. A capped months-since-inversion-end rule is a free parameter chosen against today’s known value of twenty-two. An H-window binary indicator throws away the depth variation shown in E1. A cumulative sum lacks a pre-existing definition and double-counts duration and depth across only nine episodes. Q3 is answered: no fitted model.

If the council overrules the no-shadow position, the fallback is a linear combination of curve and curve_min12 standardized on the operational calibration snapshot’s training origins with λ=1. The same NBER-onset labels, eligibility rules, and September refit apply. Memory does not replace curve.

Pre-2027 fitting is permitted only under §8.3 disclosure. The specification must state that the feature, horizon, and decision to fit were fixed after E1–E4, the August grand review, and the October 2026 backtest were known; that H=12 was already known to equal +0.24 at the 2026-09 input; and that no coefficient from this fit is evidence.

Standardization is computed on each refit snapshot using only eligible training origins whose label window is fully observed, matching operational eligibility. The z-score is (x − mean)/sd.

The live origin must be excluded from the standardization mean and variance. Q4 settles on hovedbog.jsonl with the field name curve_min12, not p_hukommelse, because Rasmus reads that file and a p_* prefix would misread the value as a probability. Q5 is unscored and carries no bar; this council does not seal a scored comparison.

Pinning a bar today after seeing every historical onset and today’s E2 reopens feature search. §8.3 requires the bar to be sealed before any run it would judge, so the symmetric bar belongs to a future council that has not just shopped the horizon against the data. Claude’s 1.96·SD_block is a reasonable future bar, but it should not be adopted today.

The 1.96·SD_block bar is incoherent because the block standard deviation is unknown for eight onsets, and normality of a two-onset difference is unverifiable. Even two post-sealing onsets cannot resolve a thirty percentage point skill gap. A bar that fires on noise or stays silent is not decisive. The honest alternative is to require at least two onsets and explicitly state that this threshold will not be decisive.

Q6 is answered: do not start a fitted shadow in November 2026. The raw curve_min12 value is already fixed at +0.24, so no parameter needs estimation yet. A fitted shadow should wait for the September 2027 refit, and this council should not seal a bar today. I will sharpen the critique of Claude’s “prospective evidence” claim.

Claude’s claim that a fitted shadow P would provide prospective evidence is rejected. The coefficient was chosen after observing all twelve onsets, so the probability is misspecified rather than genuinely prospective. Only post-sealing onsets remain, but two such onsets are too few and too distant to settle the hypothesis.

The monthly log is a monitoring series, not an experiment. Probabilities risk being promoted; yield spreads remain factual.

Claude’s claim that every historical onset came within nine months of its inversion end is incorrect. The 1957, 1960, and 1990 onsets occurred without any preceding inversion lasting at least three months.

The nine-month lag from inversion end to onset means the 12-month minimum window still contains the inversion at the origin. curve_min12 would therefore be negative at that origin, not a yield spread.

The 2008 inversion ended in April 2007, so the last origin before its January 2008 onset falls in October–December 2007. That six-to-eight-month lag is well inside the twelve-month window, confirming that curve_min12 would still be negative at that pre-onset origin.

The 2001 and 2020 onsets are also captured by H=12 at their last pre-onset origins. The 1990 onset is uncertain because the brief describes the preceding dip as shallow and brief. The horizon therefore covers the three re-steepening onsets but not the current twenty-two-month lag.

The ninety-month memory hypothesis is already the historical pattern. The open question is whether memory lasts longer than twelve months, and curve_min12 cannot answer that. This is the decisive kill shot on Claude’s Q2. I am now drafting the full proposal under the word limit, including the exact logging procedure if the council concedes a shadow model.

The concrete formula for curve_min12 is the minimum of the GS10 minus TB3MS spread across the prior eleven months, requiring at least six observations. The live value as of September 2026 is +0.24.

A logit fallback is drafted but explicitly recommended not to be computed: z-score both curve and curve_min12 on each snapshot, regress their sum with a constant on the NBER-onset label using L2-logit and λ=1, then invert the result. This remains an overruled fallback only.

The fallback regression uses the same L2-logit objective and λ=1 as the operational model, with one standardized column appended to the design matrix. The intercept is unpenalized, matching the operational model’s −0.2915 constant and single slope.

The draft is being trimmed to 1000–1100 words. The final positions are now fixed: Q1 is a flat refusal, and Q2 is a conditional specification that pins H=12 on the pre-existing definition plus the nine-month historical maximum.

The "silent today" reason is struck. Q3 rejects fitting a shadow model; the fallback is stated precisely with mandatory contamination disclosure. Q4 forbids any dashboard, LOG.md, or p_ field, and names curve_min12 in hovedbog.jsonl. The distribution argument extends to any field whose name or presentation implies a probability. Q5 keeps no scored test or bar sealed by this council; Claude’s ≥2 and "never automatic switch" constraints are future rules, not today’s evidence.

The single biggest risk is that the council discards the only cheap prospective instrument. If a future recession arrives with both curve and min12 positive, the ledger will show no paired series to demonstrate what a memory model would have predicted.
